subject: Food Science
title: Pellagra Mystery
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pellagra Mystery usable.

hook.text: In the early 1900s, pellagra killed over 100,000 Americans—mostly poor Southerners eating corn-based diets.

buildup.text: Pellagra causes the '4 Ds': dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia, and death.

discovery.text: Joseph Goldberger proved in 1915 that pellagra was dietary.

twist.text: Mexican populations eating the same corn diet had no pellagra. They treated corn with lime water (nixtamalization).

climax.text: Niacin (vitamin B3) enrichment of flour was mandated in 1941. Pellagra vanished from the US within a decade.

punchline.text: Corn locked niacin away. Mexico's ancient process freed it.

quiz.question: Why didn't Mexican populations get pellagra from corn-based diets?
options: Nixtamalization (treating corn with lime water) releases bound niacin—a 3,500-year-old process
